headline: Un registro de deudores por terrorismo se hará realidad
content: La Comisión de Justicia del Congreso aprobó ayer el proyecto de ley que crea el registro de deudores de reparaciones civiles por delitos de terrorismo y corrupción.  La información la dio a conocer el presidente de esa comisión, Juan Carlos Eguren, quien precisó que el Estado ha sufrido daños y perjuicios económicos por más de S/.4.817 millones por la acción del terrorismo y la corrupción.  En este registro se inscribirán a las personas deudoras de reparaciones civiles provenientes.

headline: Humala: La tarea de reformar el Estado es un pedido a gritos
content: Nos hemos trazado [...] la tarea de reformar el Estado. Un pedido a gritos. Todo el país quiere un Estado moderno, eficiente, donde el servidor sea realmente servidor de los ciudadanos y no que se sirvan de nosotros, acotó el mandatario cuando afronta los niveles más bajos de popularidad.  Explicó que para alcanzar este objetivo, su gobierno ha iniciado reformas en los sectores educación, militar, policial, tributario, servicio civil y ahora en el sector salud: Porque sabemos que así como vamos avanzando a un ritmo de crecimiento del país [...] necesitamos también entender que dentro de algunos años todos vamos a querer más calidad en los servicios, por lo tanto el Estado actual tiene que ser reformado.

headline: Homage to Bedoya Reyes
content: Under the motto The democracy in our hands, the National Jury of Elections (JNE) commemorates tomorrow International Democracy Day in Plaza San Martin. In this celebration, special homage will be paid to the founder of the PPC, Luis Bedoya Reyes, for his defense of democracy in Peru, according to details provided by the JNE.

headline: Also goes Fujimoris turn
content: Today at noon, former presidential candidate Pedro Pablo Kuczynski will meet with Prime Minister Juan Jiménez, as part of dialogue with the government. According to PPK, he will bring seven measures that should be implemented to ensure economic growth. His party, Per Más, along with its technicians including Beatriz Merino, will accompany him. At five in the afternoon, it’s FPs turn led by their secretary-general Jaime Yoshiyama. This concludes the first round of discussions.

headline: Drug trafficking under scrutiny
content: According to Masas, everyone is concerned because drug trafficking is a global plague [...] Nobody is untouchable, we have to remain open to being audited, observed. However, she clarified what cannot happen is accusing someone without presenting evidence that would justify such claims.

headline: Charges Against Ex-Fiscal General
content: Former Attorney General Gladys Echaíz accused Sergio Tejada, head of the mega commission investigating Alan Garcías administration, of leaking preliminary reports concerning the Business Track case to media outlets—a move described as both grave and malicious. She argued these documents essentially serve as defenses for members of company BTR, echoing arguments found within rulings made by higher courts which constitute final judgments.

headline: An Accused Candidate Faces Allegations
content: Professor Alejandro Guzmán Álvarez, running for city council through the Christian Peoples Party (PPC), was charged by parents claiming inappropriate behavior towards three nine-year-old students at school José Carlos Mariategui in Huancayo. Following allegations involving gifts and physical contact during meetings where children sat on his lap, authorities initiated legal proceedings leading to his removal from teaching positions despite ongoing employment elsewhere.

headline: Notary Involved in Corruption Inquiry Set to Testify
content: Melvin Rudelman, who facilitated the establishment of consulting firm Ecotecsa Consulting, is scheduled to testify before prosecutor Elizabeth Parco next month via video conference from Costa Rica. Initially planned for July 16th, the session was postponed pending review of statements previously submitted in his home country. Rudelman confirmed requests from former President Toledo to establish Ecotecsa back in January 2012.

headline: Conflict Over District Boundaries Between San Isidro and Magdalena
content: Following disputes over jurisdiction between districts, the Constitutional Court urged the Metropolitan Municipality of Lima to resolve boundary issues rather than entertain individual district complaints like those filed by San Isidro seeking cessation of property certifications issued by neighboring Magdalena. Both parties involved continue negotiations mediated by the Institute of Urban Planning while awaiting legislative action defining precise boundaries across affected areas.

headline: New Services Available For Disabled Residents Of Pacachique
content: Approximately 1,000 disabled residents of Ventanilla received equipment aimed at improving mobility thanks to efforts coordinated by the Disability Council alongside international NGO Plan International.

headline: Mayor Addresses Museum Management Concerns
content: In response to criticisms surrounding management practices at the Metropolitan Museum managed by Iguana Films, Mayor Susana Villarán explained delays encountered acquiring specific lighting fixtures necessary for exhibits covering half of museum space requiring imports unavailable locally. Efforts underway aim to complete installations ensuring full operational status shortly thereafter.

headline: Traffic Challenges During Festival Mistura
content: Yesterday saw significant traffic congestion around Coastal Greenway near Miraflores caused largely by visitors attending culinary festival Mistura resulting in extensive vehicle queues stretching beyond designated parking facilities prompting police intervention albeit limited success managing flow effectively amidst high visitor turnout.

headline: Escándalo en la Municipalidad de Lima
content: Lima pagará S/.3700.000 porque Relima  y Emmsa olvidaron firmar el contrato  Empresa de limpieza ingres al mercado de Santa Anita sin pasar por concurso público. Ahora pide pago que triplica costo real del servicio.  Durante siete meses los funcionarios de Emmsa omitieron contratar la limpieza en el nuevo mercado mayorista. Dejaron que Relima lo hiciera por su cuenta y ahora esta pide un pago mayor. Aún así, en abril y julio se adjudicó el servicio a la misma empresa.

headline: Opinión
content: Otra deuda que derivó en ilícito  Johnny Zás Fríz Abogado especializado en Derecho Pblico.  En situaciones de emergencia, la ley permite que la prestación de un servicio sea regularizada hasta dos meses después de haberse iniciado y bajo la modalidad de adjudicación directa por desabastecimiento inminente. Pero eso no ocurrió aquí. No se comunicó a la OSCE ni se regularizó el contrato hasta siete meses después. Esto se resume en una omisión de funciones e incumplimiento de la Ley de Contrataciones, más aún en una empresa con autonomía económica y administrativa. Está situación se solventará mediante un arbitraje o un juicio.

headline: Política
content: Voceros parlamentarios deciden pronta elección de los tres directores del BCR  Qued en manos del Presidente del Congreso la formulación de la comisión calificadora que llevará a los nominados a la Plenaria.  El Consejo Directivo del Congreso aprobó ayer que la elección de los tres directores del Banco Central de Reserva (BCR) se realice lo más pronto posible. Luego seguirán la elección de los seis magistrados del Tribunal Constitucional y del defensor del pueblo.

headline: Punto de Vista
content: Primera señal del dialogo?  Ha hecho dos días, el mismo Otrola plantee—a través de El Comercio—a sus demás colegas parlamentarios las características del perfil de las nuevas autoridades por seleccionarse: extenso conocimiento jurídico, una trayectoria limpia y, idealmente, sin afiliación política activa.  Nadie se opone a esos requisitos, pero estamos en el Congreso Peruano, coment con ironía el representante Aprista Mauricio Mulder.
